headline: Adaptability is changing when conditions change—the skill that lets you survive shifts you can't control
universal_truth: The world changes; those who adjust thrive while those who resist struggle
fun_facts: Darwin never said 'survival of the fittest'—he emphasized survival of the most adaptable
Companies that pivot (change direction) based on feedback are more likely to succeed than those that stick rigidly to plans
The human brain's plasticity means we can learn new skills at any age
discussion_questions: What change are you currently resisting?
When has adapting served you well?
How do you balance persistence with adaptability?

hook.script: Dinosaurs dominated for 165 million years—then conditions changed. Small, adaptable mammals survived the asteroid; giant dinosaurs didn't. In evolution and in life, it's not the strongest or smartest who survive—it's those who adapt.

cliff.script: We just talked about persistence—but sometimes stubbornness kills. How do you know when to persist and when to adapt? They seem like opposites.

options.text: Persist on goals and values, adapt on methods and tactics—be firm about where you're going, flexible about how you get there
options.response: Yes. Your destination stays fixed; your route changes. When the path is blocked, you don't abandon the goal—you find another way. Rigidity on strategy, flexibility on tactics.

options.text: Adapt when you've tried everything possible and nothing works
options.response: That's one signal, but the best adapters change earlier—when feedback suggests a better path...

fact1.title: Feedback Sensitivity
fact1.script: Adaptable people are sensitive to feedback. They notice when something isn't working before they've invested too much. They treat early failure as information, not defeat. Sensitivity to signals enables timely change.

fact2.title: Sunk Cost Release
fact2.script: Past investment ('sunk cost') shouldn't dictate future decisions, but we often cling to failing paths because of what we've already spent. Adaptable people cut losses. They ask 'what should I do now?' not 'how much have I invested?'

fact3.title: Identity Flexibility
fact3.script: Sometimes adapting means changing who you think you are. 'I'm not a tech person' becomes a prison. Adaptable people hold identity loosely—they can become whatever circumstances require. You're not stuck being who you were.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The world changes. Adaptability teaches that those who adjust thrive while those who resist struggle. Hold your goals firmly and your methods loosely.

outro.script: That's Day 189. Tomorrow, we'll explore bouncing back—resilience. Until then, identify one thing that's changed around you that you haven't yet adapted to.

growTrack.title: Adaptation Audit - What's Changed?
growTrack.activity: List three things that have changed in your work, relationships, or environment in the last year. For each, ask: Have I adapted, or am I still operating as if things were the same? What adjustment would help?
